chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far (peace be upon him), who said:

One of you takes comfort from the oil, and water is more expansive than that. Shall I narrate to you the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)? I said, ‘Yes’. He said, ‘So he entered his hand into the vessel and did not wash his hand, but he took a palmful of water and poured it upon his face. Then he wiped its two sides until he had wiped all of it. Then he took another palmful with his right hand and poured it upon his left side, then washed with it his right arm. Then he took another palmful and washed with it his left arm. Then he wiped his head and his feet with whatever remained in his hand.’

key_terms.الدُّهْنِ: Oil or fat (used as a metaphor for comfort)
key_terms.جَانِبَيْهِ: Its two sides (referring to the face)
key_terms.كَفّاً: Palmful (a measure of water held in the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific method of performing ablution (wudu) as demonstrated by the Messenger of Allah in this narration?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic practice of pouring water directly from the hand into the vessel without pre-washing, a detail often discussed in Shia fiqh regarding the sufficiency of water contact. It emphasizes the methodical application of water to the face, arms, head, and feet, reinforcing the ritual purity (taharah) described in Surah al-Ma'idah. The narration serves as a practical guide for believers to emulate the exact manner in which the Prophet performed wudu, ensuring the validity of their prayers.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘One of you takes comfort from the oil, so he fills his body with it, and the water is more expansive than that. Shall Iasws imitate for you all an Ablution (Wudhu) of Rasool-Allahsaww?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So heasws entered hisasws hand into the vessel and did not wash hisasws hand, but heasws grabbed a palm-full of water and poured it upon hisasws face. Then heasws wiped its two (facial) sides until heasws had wiped all of it. Then heasws grabbled another (palm-full) with hisasws left hand and heasws poured it upon hisasws right hand. Then heasws washed it hisasws right arm. Then heasws grabbed another palm-full, so heasws washed with it hisasws left arm. Then heasws wiped hisasws head and hisasws feet with whatever remained in hisasws hand’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said, ‘

When one of you wants to mb oil over his body, he does so only with some oil in the palm of his hand and covers his whole body. Water, however, is more plentiful. Do you want me to demonstrate how the Messenger of Allah would take Wudu’?’ I said, ‘Please do so.’ He (the Imam) then placed his hand in the water but did not wash his hand. He (the Imam) then with some water in the palm of his hand, allowed it to flow down his face and then wiped both sides of his face until he wiped it all. He (the Imam) then with some water in the palm of his right hand, poured it on the palm of his left hand and with it he washed his right forearm. He (the Imam) with some water in the palm of his right hand, washed his left forearm. He (the Imam) then with whatever water was left on his hands, wiped his head and feet.”
